name: Pantoprazole
sections: White to off-white crystalline powder (sodium sesquihydrate), freely soluble in water.

Has lower affinity for CYP enzymes than omeprazole, giving fewer drug interactions; preferred PPI with clopidogrel. First approval/introduction: Research began 1985 (Byk Gulden); Germany 1994; US FDA 2000 (Wyeth).

Irreversibly inhibits H+/K+-ATPase in gastric parietal cells, suppressing basal and stimulated acid secretion. Receptor / target profile: Prodrug activated in acidic canaliculi; covalently binds cysteine residues of H+/K+-ATPase.
Summary: Bioavailability ~77%; Tmax 2–3 h (enteric-coated). ~98% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. Half-life ~1 h (effect lasts >24 h).
Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and erosive oesophagitis – healing and maintenance
GERD / ulcer: 40 mg once daily before breakfast for 4–8 weeks
H. pylori: 40 mg twice daily with appropriate antibiotics
Swallow whole 30–60 min before a meal
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Severe: max 20 mg/day (some labels 40 mg alternate days).
EE with GERD ≥5 years: 20–40 mg/day by weight.
Hypersensitivity to pantoprazole or substituted benzimidazoles
Long-term use: hypomagnesaemia, vitamin B12 deficiency, fractures
C. difficile diarrhoea, subacute cutaneous lupus
Drugs needing gastric acid for absorption (ketoconazole, atazanavir, iron salts)
Magnesium on long-term use; B12 on long-term use.
COMPASS (Moayyedi et al., Gastroenterology 2019) – pantoprazole reduced bleeding from gastroduodenal lesions in patients on anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy.
Lower CYP2C19 interaction potential – preferred PPI with clopidogrel.
Swallow whole – do not crush or chew
Do not use long-term without review
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
